question: Find the amount (integral value only) if a sum of ₹6,500 is being borrowed at 10% interest per annum for 2 years if interest is compounded half-yearly
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rate per half-year = 10% ÷ 2 = 5%

Effective CI rate for 4 cycles of 5% ≈ 21.55%

Amount = Principal × (100% + Effective Rate)

Amount = 6500 × 121.55% = 6500 × 1.2155 ≈ 7900.75

The nearest integral value is ₹7,900.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7,900.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹6,500

Rate of Interest (R) = 10% per annum

Time (T) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ

Where r is the rate per period and n is the number of periods.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since interest is compounded half-yearly, r = 10% ÷ 2 = 5%.

⇒ Number of half-years (n) = 2 × 2 = 4 cycles.

⇒ A = 6500 × (1 + 5/100)⁴

⇒ A = 6500 × (105/100)⁴

⇒ A = 6500 × (21/20)⁴

⇒ A = 6500 × (194481 ÷ 160000)

⇒ A = 65 × (194481 ÷ 1600) = 12641265 ÷ 1600

⇒ A ≈ 7900.79

⇒ Taking the required integral value, the amount becomes ₹7,900.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7,900.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Quarterly Compounding

When interest is compounded quarterly, the given annual rate is divided by 4 (R/4) and the time periods are multiplied by 4 (4T).

Effective Rate Formula

The effective compound interest rate for 2 continuous cycles at a rate R% is given by R + R + (R × R)/100.

Simple vs Compound Interest

Simple Interest (SI) remains constant for each period, whereas Compound Interest (CI) increases exponentially as interest is calculated on both principal and accumulated interest.
